notes:
Account summary: enterprise telco focused on low-latency customer-facing AI features (support chat & intent reranking). Strong ops team; procurement and legal are risk-averse. Primary goal: move critical chat stack from hosted to Dedicated with strict SLOs and a clear DR/fallback plan.

Key technical requirements (from SE call and traffic samples):
- Target p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 120ms for short chat turns (~64 tokens). P99 target <= 250ms.
- Sustained throughput target 200 req/s for chat endpoints; peak bursts up to 1.2k req/s during promotions.
- Embeddings pipeline: 3k qps offline embedding jobs; can be batched with 2s latency window.
- Reranking workload: heavy CPU+KV-cache reuse; tight tail latency requirements (p95 < 80ms).
- Model preference: base on Redwood-verified LLMs; primary model = "redwood-3-large" quantized (8-bit) in production; fallback variants = r3-medium (lower cost) and r3-small for extreme saturation.

Dedicated / capacity planning notes:
- Initial reserved plan proposed by Redwood: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching and a hot-standby pair in another region for cross-region failover. Estimated sustained token/sec capacity meets 200 req/s for 64-token median.
- Autoscaling policy: reserved low-latency pool + burst capacity to public cluster governed by policy with model-variant fallback if burst > 2x baseline.
- KV/prefix caching: propose hot prefix cache replication to standby region for sub-second cold-starts on failover.
- Warm-up / slot allocation: recommend pre-warming KV caches for top 500 prefixes (support flows).

Reliability & fallback design (discussion points + AE notes):
- Cross-region failover: Hawthorn requires documented RTO/RPO. Proposed approach: active-active for control-plane (configsync + incremental state sync), active-passive for inference with pre-warmed hot-standby region. Failover steps: 1) health detection -> 2) routing shift -> 3) model variant ramp -> 4) capacity autoscale. Target detection to route shift < 5 minutes.
- Model variant fallback: policy-driven routing that demotes requests to r3-medium when p95 exceeds threshold, while preserving response format and function calling behavior. Must ensure deterministic quality checks and telemetry.
- Graceful degradation: for extreme saturation, tiered degradation: reduce max generation tokens, increase caching TTL, switch to lower-parameter model. Need explicit user-facing messaging plan for degraded quality windows.

SLA negotiations / commercial notes:
- Hawthorn asks for a 99.9% availability SLA for dedicated inference endpoints with credits for missed latency SLOs at p95 and p99 windows. Legal flagged cross-region liability for data residency — need term edits.
- Pricing sensitivity: prefers fixed monthly committed spend with burst credits. ARR target for first year in forecast band; negotiating 12-24 month reserved commitment.

Open action items (short):
- SE (Rosa) to share detailed sizing workbook based on 30-day traces (due 2026-02-10).
- AE (Liam) to get procurement budget confirmation and share draft term sheet (due 2026-02-18).
- Run DR tabletop: schedule cross-region failover simulation with Hawthorn infra team (propose 2026-03-02).
- Legal to propose SLA amendments on data residency and failover liability (ticket SEC-1178).

Stated quotes from CTO on 2026-01-12 call: "We need guaranteed tail latency for support chat — if we lose that we lose customer trust. We'll accept minor quality degradation during bursts but need clear playbooks."
